text.p: Italian bonds and futures slid just before the close after a late recovery on a Treasuries rally on talk the EU accounting commission had ruled against French deficit-reduction plans to meet EMU criteria, traders said.

Traders in both London and Milan referred to a report that the accounting commission had expressed an opinion against the French government's plans to switch funds from France Telecom to the state. Such adjustment of accounts ahead of entry into the single currency has been criticised as "window-dressing".
"Just the Italian and Spanish markets fell but not the French, it's very strange," said one London trader
Italian bonds and futures had earlier risen in late trade to make up all the day's losses in an about turn on a rally on T-bonds after favourable economic data, traders said.

Btps tracked bunds lower in the morning on a series of statements that Germany might not meet Maastricht debt and deficit criteria, seesawing views on whether the Bundesbank should raise rates, and the Buba's Koebnick saying he didn't think the mark would fall further over the next two years.
The lira weakened and the Btp Dec contract touched a low of 122.39. "But everything turned positive in the afternoon when Treasuries rallied on U.S. data," one trader said.
